feedback: Iteration 0 is the only raced evidence. All 60 trials went off track on oval, s-bend and slalom (0 finishes). Progress stalled at 0.10 to 0.14, max_error reached 0.062 to 0.064 (just past the 0.06 m limit), and line_loss_events was 1.0 in every trial. RMS error was low (0.026 to 0.030) and steering_oscillation was low (0.08 to 0.14). That pattern points to the robot being too loose and too fast to hold the tape through bends, not to jitter. The candidate responds to that: base_speed 1.6 to 1.4, kp 2.5 to 3.5, kd 0.15 to 0.3, a small ki of 0.1 to remove the roughly 2 percent motor-mismatch bias, and sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016. The candidate is valid: all sensor positions are in range, sensor_size 0.016 is an allowed option, and the weights and line_loss are allowed. Nothing is obviously broken. Its weak points are that it changes five things at once, so the next race will not show which change mattered, and that the sensor footprints at 0.016 m with 0.02 m spacing now overlap. I cannot say how it will perform, only that it addresses the observed failure. Approve it now: this is early exploration, the baseline has zero finishes, and the race telemetry is needed more than another round of reading numbers. Next race, read the results as follows. If line_loss_events is still 1.0 or max_error is still above 0.06, the robot is still leaving the line. Then cut base_speed to 1.2 and keep kp at 3.5, since the speed is the likeliest cause. If line_loss_events is 0 or near 0 and steering_oscillation stays under about 0.15, but completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 (for example 1.5) and keep kd at 0.3. If the robot oscillates (steering_oscillation above 0.2), lower kp to about 3.0 before changing anything else.
requested_changes: If the next race still shows line_loss_events of 1.0 or more and max_error above 0.06 on the oval or slalom, lower base_speed from 1.4 to 1.2 and keep kp at 3.5, kd at 0.3 and ki at 0.1 (iteration 0 lost the line at base_speed 1.6 with kp 2.5).

If the run is clean (line_loss_events near 0, steering_oscillation under 0.15) but completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 toward 1.5 and keep kd at 0.3 (completion_time was not reached in iteration 0, so this is a hypothesis to test).
If steering_oscillation rises above 0.2 with kp 3.5, lower kp to 3.0 and keep kd at 0.3, since kd 0.15 at iteration 0 left oscillation at 0.08 to 0.14 and kd has not yet been tested at 0.3.
